description: We are thrilled to be participating in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. Together, we are pooling our collective talents to build something meaningful.

They keep them alive. Team Axe built an open-source decision-support pipeline (teamaxe/lunar) that translates lunar south pole orbital data into easiealy understable factors: vehicle, parking and location condition
​Our pipeline ingests NASA LRO LOLA and USGS 118m DEM topography, reconciles Principal Axis to Mean Earth frames using PGDA LOLA products, and computes 360° horizon occlusion, solar illumination (Mazarico et al., 2011), and Direct-to-Earth libration windows via JPL Horizons and NAIF SPICE DE440 kernels. Thermal envelopes and Permanently Shadowed Region cold traps are validated against LRO Diviner observations (Paige et al., 2010) and Chandrayaan-3 ChaSTE regolith conductivity benchmarks, with basemaps streamed via NASA Moon Trek WMTS.

The intended outcome is a unified planning interface that makes important lunar environmental constraints easier to explore, interpret, and compare.

details: At the Moon's south pole, steep craters, long shadows, and freezing temperatures can end a mission before it starts. Team Axe built an open-source Lunar Landing Site Navigator that turns NASA elevation maps, JPL orbit forecasts, LRO Diviner thermal data, and Chandrayaan-3 ground measurements into simple GO, MARGINAL, or NO-GO ratings. In seconds, planners can verify safe slopes, sunlight, Earth radio contact, and short paths to icy craters.
